ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (as revised in 2020); Administrative Measures for the Information Registration of Beneficial Owners of Market Entities (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation, Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar in the investor's domicile (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State, or commercial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary public; then either (i) obtain a Hague Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state if that state is an Apostille Convention party, or (ii) undergo local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate if that state is not an Apostille party. These two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of the foreign investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authoritative government registry or corporate registrar in the investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same dual-path notarization and apostille or consular legalization procedure as the Certificate of Incorporation; the document must be issued no earlier than 90 days before the SAMR filing date.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE legal representative and local agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor's board of directors and a duly authorized notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Board resolution must be certified by the company secretary or notary; then apostille or consular legalization depending on the Apostille Convention membership of the investor's jurisdiction; followed by certified Chinese translation by a SAMR-recognized translation agency.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the foreign investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investing company as adopted and certified by the company secretary or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy of the constitutional documents; apostille or consular legalization as applicable under the investment jurisdiction; certified Chinese translation required for SAMR records.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming investor banking relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank in the investor's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter must bear original bank seal and authorized signatory certification; notarized by a local notary; then apostille or consular legalization as applicable; certified Chinese translation needed. The bank reference must explicitly cover source of funds for AML/CFT purposes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must be screened against the PRC domestic Politically Exposed Persons database, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists (1267/1988 and 1718), the U.S. OFAC SDN List, EU restrictive measures, and the People's Bank of China blacklist and sanctioned-party repositories. Screening must be repeated at formation and updated every 24 hours until incorporation is complete, and then continuously upon any ownership or management change. Any positive match requires escalation to the AML compliance officer, enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds investigation, and rejection where sanctions exposure is not rebuttable. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration and Online Clearance System (gsxt.gov.cn enterprise name declaration module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered Chinese-language company name must follow the four-tier statutory format: Administrative Division + Distinctive Trade Name + Industry Description + Company Form. Only simplified Chinese characters are accepted; traditional Chinese characters and non-Chinese scripts cannot form the main legal name. A phonetic transliteration of the foreign investor's trade name is permitted in simplified characters and must be consistent with business scope. An English name may be registered as a secondary name but does not replace the official Chinese legal name. All characters must be typed and verified against the SAMR prohibited-name database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of name rejection, the applicant must receive a written rejection notice citing the statutory grounds. Within 15 working days from receipt, the applicant may submit a written administrative reconsideration application to the SAMR superior authority or the local people's government, seeking reversal of the refusal. Alternatively, an administrative lawsuit may be filed in the competent people's court within six months. The appeal should include a revised name draft that eliminates the prohibited tokens, supporting notarized identity and corporate documents, and, if applicable, a petition for ministerial authorization of a sensitive token. Pre-filing consultation with the registration office is strongly recommended to shorten the correction cycle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A fully virtual or post-mail-only address is not acceptable for a WFOE in the wholesale bitumen and asphalt logistics trading sector. SAMR requires a real, rentable, and verifiable commercial premises; while some free trade zones permit registered office listings, tax authorities, banks, and customs will reject a purely virtual address for obtaining a VAT invoice quota, opening a corporate bank account, or completing customs registration for containerized goods. The entity must maintain a physical lease, a dedicated office or licensed storage facility, and at least one on-site employee. Shared or incubation addresses are treated as high-risk and typically trigger enhanced due diligence and a physical inspection by the tax authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) signed office lease with rent receipts; (ii) presence of staff during operational hours; (iii) utility and internet invoices addressed to the registered premises; (iv) business signage or reception capacity; (v) import/export records for bitumen containers; (vi) corporate bank account statements reflecting commercial substance. Quantified risk: approximately 30% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the local SAMR or tax authority, increasing to 40% if the office is shared, if VAT invoice issuance is unexpectedly high, or if the entity has zero employees. Non-satisfaction of any checklist item may trigger immediate license suspension or refusal of name and registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) enterprise name clearance and business license filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (People's Republic of China)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official registration fee is charged for ordinary company incorporation and name reservation; statutory no-fee policy.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Apostille, and/or Consular Legalization of five mandatory corporate instruments of the foreign investor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local notary public, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Chinese Embassy/Consulate (or competent apostille authority)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing international market benchmark for notarization plus apostille at USD 100-250 per document; consular legalization fees per embassy schedule and variable expedite charges.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of corporate records, constitutional documents, and UBO declaration package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 0.05-0.10 per Chinese character or USD 15-25 per standard page; total estimated for 8-10 pages.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical commercial registered office lease deposit and first quarter rent (non-virtual)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private landlord or licensed commercial business center
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing municipal industrial/trade zone monthly rent of USD 600-1,000; deposit equal to two months' rent; total first quarter and deposit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seals and legal representative authorization documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory public security fee for engraving company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal; market benchmark USD 100-200.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC legal counsel retainer for incorporation, name clearance, UBO filing, and AML/CFT screening protocol implementation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm licensed by the Ministry of Justice (PRC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market flat fee for WFOE incorporation and due diligence package inclusive of PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 beneficial ownership filing; hourly rates USD 100-300 per hour if ad hoc.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Chapter II, Limited Companies, Articles 128, 129, 131, 133, 148, 156, 161-1, and 387-1; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Article 7; Investment Commission Regulations on Foreign Investment Approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, Company Registration One-Stop Service; Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration together with the Articles of Incorporation and supporting corporate resolutions, resulting in issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation by the MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Taiwan Company Act; the incorporating shareholder may fix the initial capital in the Articles. Paid-in cash capital must be remitted to a temporary Taiwan bank account before registration and verified by a Taiwan certified public accountant. No statutory blocked escrow account is required beyond this pre-registration capital deposit and CPA verification obligation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD (the Company), a Taiwan limited company, held at [address] on [date], at [time], Taipei time. Present: [director names], constituting a quorum. The Chairman stated that all formalities preliminary to the incorporation were completed, including the receipt of the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs approval letter, execution of the Articles of Incorporation, and deposit and verification of the Company capital. After deliberation, the Board unanimously adopted the following resolutions: 1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUE OF SHARE CAPITAL. RESOLVED, that the initial registered capital of the Company is hereby fixed at US$[amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares of par value US$[par] each, all of which have been subscribed and fully paid by the sole shareholder prior to incorporation; the certified public accountant capital verification report shall be conclusive evidence of payment; the Chairman and General Manager are authorized to issue share certificates and to take all actions necessary to declare the share capital as paid in the files of the Ministry of Economic Affairs. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open operating, foreign currency, and payroll bank accounts with [bank name], Taiwan; that the authorized signatories shall be the Chairman, General Manager, and Chief Financial Officer, with the signature of any two of them required for each withdrawal, letter of credit, wire transfer, or acceptance instrument; and that the Chairman is authorized to execute the relevant account resolutions, mandate letters, signature cards, and bank forms. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be at [address], Taiwan; the Chairman and legal counsel are authorized to execute the lease, include the address in notices and corporate stationery, and perfect any change of address required by law. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [name] be and hereby is appointed Chairman and Representative Director; [name], General Manager; [name], Chief Financial Officer; and [name], Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering Officer. The General Manager shall supervise daily operations and trade documentation for bitumen wholesale and logistics; the Chief Financial Officer shall maintain corporate books, file tax returns and financial reports, and act as principal liaison to the National Taxation Bureau and foreign exchange banks; the Compliance Officer shall implement KYC, AML, sanctions screening, customs declarations, and counterparty due diligence for SWIFT LC and TT wire payment rails. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION AND RATIFICATION. RESOLVED, that all actions taken by the incorporators, attorneys, and officers before the date of this resolution in connection with formation, capitalization, and licensing are ratified, approved, and confirmed; and that any officer or counsel is authorized to execute and deliver any further agreements, certificates, or notifications as may be required by the registry, banking institutions, tax authorities, or other regulators. ADOPTED by the unanimous consent of the Board of Directors on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Investor Qualification Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan — Online Foreign Investor Application Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for approval under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, identifying the ultimate beneficial owner, source of funds, investment amount, and intended business scope as ISIC 4661 wholesale supply of drummed and bagged penetration-grade bitumen. Where the investor is a foreign company, the certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and board resolution authorizing the WFOE investment must be authenticated by a Taiwanese overseas representative office or notarized; all non-Chinese documents must be translated into English/Chinese and notarized. Engage a local Taiwan counsel to verify capital entry paths and obtain Investment Commission approval letter before filing company registration. Use the online portal to upload PDF dossiers and pay the processing fee via online transfer.
required_dossiers: Online foreign investor application form
Authenticated certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of the ultimate investor
Board resolution of the foreign investor approving the WFOE establishment and capital subscription
Bank statement or asset verification showing lawful source of funds
Investment plan and business scope description (ISIC 4661 / NAICS 424720)
Power of attorney and local representative identification
Notarized English/Chinese translation of all corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query or requests supplemental information, cure within the statutory response period by submitting a supplemental letter through the portal; if approval is refused, file an administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan within 30 days of service after correcting any due-diligence deficiencies and re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, MOEA — Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System (one-stop service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for advance approval of the Chinese and English company names and the precise business scope text. The business scope must include wholesale trading of bitumen and asphalt products, containerized storage, and logistics for imported bitumen to align with ISIC 4661 and NAICS 424720. Submit an application with the pre-approved foreign-investment letter and proposed articles. The name should not conflict with registered companies, preferred corporate names, or trademarks. After approval, the name reservation is valid for six months and is renewable once; any change in the business scope requires a new application. The registry will issue an electronic name pre-review certificate.
required_dossiers: Company name and business scope pre-review application form
Foreign investment approval letter from the Investment Commission, MOEA
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney for local formation agent
List of proposed Chinese and English company names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, select the next reserved alternative from the list and re-file within three business days; if the scope is deemed imprecise, amend the activity wording to mirror the Investment Commission approval and resubmit through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation; Capital Deposit and Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators meeting and designated Taiwan bank; registration thereafter is through the Department of Commerce, MOEA One-Stop Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal counsel drafts the Articles of Incorporation consistent with the Investment Commission approval and name certificate. The sole incorporator executes the articles and subscribes the share capital; capital is paid into a newly opened temporary corporate bank account at a Taiwan bank in TWD or USD and verified by a certified public accountant in Taiwan. The CPA issues a capital verification report certifying full payment before registration. The articles must set out corporate name, object, capital, registered office, number of directors, method of representation, and duration. The first director s execute a consent to appointment; the resolution of the first board is prepared. Keep the bank receipt and CPA report for filing.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation signed by incorporating shareholder
Minutes of the incorporation/subscription meeting
Capital verification report issued by a Taiwan certified public accountant
Bank deposit receipt or passbook of the temporary capital account
Consent to act executed by each director
First Board of Directors resolution
Name pre-review certificate and foreign investment approval letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry objects to the articles or capital verification, amend the offending article and have the incorporators and CPA re-sign or re-issue; notarize corrections, then re-submit with a cover letter; if the CPA report shows defective capital remittance, cure by re-depositing funds and updating the bank attestation before formal filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, MOEA — Company Registration One-Stop Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for company registration within 15 days after the articles are executed and capital certified. Upload the complete statutory annex through the one-stop portal, including application form, articles, minutes, capital report, name certificate, director consents, registered office lease or certificate of consent, and foreign investment approval. The MOEA examines the filing for legality and enters the company into the Company and Commerce Registration Database, issuing a Certificate of Incorporation with a unified business number. For a limited company, the representative director must sign the application; if any director is unable to sign, attach a notarized proxy. After approval, the electronic company chop may be applied for; this registration also initiates tax registration through the government inter-operation data exchange.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
Articles of Incorporation and associated corporate resolutions
Capital verification report and bank deposit evidence
Company name pre-review certificate
Director consent letters and identification documents
Registered office lease or premises consent and building occupancy certificate
Foreign investment approval letter
Filing fee remittance proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a corrigendum, cure within 15 days by uploading an amended document with explanations; if the registration is rejected, petition the MOEA for administrative review within 30 days; if the defect is procedural, withdraw and re-file once corrected to avoid accruing late fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Foreign Exchange, Customs, and Labor Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Central Bank of China and authorized foreign exchange banks; Bureau of Foreign Trade, MOEA; Ministry of Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register for corporate income tax, business tax, and invoicing in the Tax Registration System; apply for tax exemption or qualified enterprise status where applicable. Open USD and NTD operating bank accounts and register with the Central Bank foreign exchange system for import and export settlement; obtain an exporter and importer registration from the Bureau of Foreign Trade so that bitumen bills of lading and LC and TT payment rails may be used. Register the foreign investor remittance with the bank and obtain the foreign currency investment remittance filing from the Central Bank. File labor insurance, health insurance, and pension enrollment for employees with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and National Health Insurance Administration; establish employment and workplace safety records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and unified business number certificate
Company chop and representative director identification
Tax registration application and capital verification report
Articles of Incorporation and bank account authorization resolution
Foreign exchange bank account opening forms and CIPRS enrollment
Exporter/importer registration application
Labor insurance, health insurance, and pension enrollment schedules
Investment remittance and foreign currency declaration due diligence pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is suspended for incomplete data, file the missing schedules through the Ministry of Finance portal and pay any late-filing surcharge; if customs registration is rejected, verify the correct HS code for bitumen and asphalt products, correct the commodity classification, and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental, Fire Safety, and Occupational Licensing for Containerized Bitumen Operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Administration, MOEA; Environmental Protection Administration; Local Fire Bureau; Ministry of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company operates a container yard, warehouse, or asphalt drum transfer station, apply for warehouse and business operation registration with the local municipal government; if storage of bitumen or asphalt products meets the dangerous goods threshold, submit a Public Hazardous Substances and Combustible Materials storage permit application to the Fire Bureau. For non-manufacturing operations, complete an environmental self-registration; for any storage facility above the statutory capacity threshold, conduct an environmental impact assessment. Prepare a fire safety plan, civil defense structural inspection by a licensed engineer, occupational emergency response plan, and train staff on hot asphalt handling hazards, H2S monitoring, spill containment, and personal protective equipment. Obtain customs bonded or non-bonded logistics approval where applicable.
required_dossiers: Warehouse or container yard business operation registration application
Fire safety equipment plan and design approval
Civil defense and structural load inspection report for storage and stacking areas
Dangerous goods or petroleum/asphalt storage facility permit application
Environmental self-registration or EIA documentation if threshold triggered
Occupational safety and health compliance audit report
Spill containment and emergency response plan
Container and storage tank inspection certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire or environmental permit is objected, perform any required engineering modifications, re-inspection, and submit a corrective action plan; if the EIA classification is raised, transition to a fuller EIA under EPA direction and extend the construction or operation timeline accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; local Municipal Bureau of Commerce or Economic Development for warehouse and business registration; local Fire Bureau for fire permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate statutory sectoral license is required for the pure wholesale trading of bitumen; however, if the Company operates a container yard, asphalt drum warehouse, or transfer station, it must obtain a Business Registration Certificate, Public Hazardous Substances and Combustible Materials Storage Permit, and a Petroleum/Asphalt Storage Facility Permit where the stored bitumen is classified as a petroleum product.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For pure wholesale trade without storage tanks or warehouse construction: Category C Environmental Registration. For operation of a container yard or warehouse dedicated to bitumen storage with floor area above 5,000 square meters, storage capacity above 10,000 cubic meters, or presence in a sensitive ecological zone, a Category B Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is mandatory; otherwise a Brief Project Environmental Assessment or environmental self-registration under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is required. If the Company uses only third-party logistics and performs no physical storage, the EIA requirement is Not Applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must meet Taiwan effluent limits: pH 6-9, biochemical oxygen demand under 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand under 100 mg/L, suspended solids under 30 mg/L, oil and grease under 10 mg/L, and hexane extract under 10 mg/L; no process or wash water may enter storm drains without pretreatment. Air emissions from hot bitumen handling or tank heating must be controlled for fugitive VOC leaks; visible black smoke shall not exceed 20% opacity during loading or cleaning operations, and fenceline VOC concentrations shall comply with applicable petroleum and petrochemical emission standards. Hazardous waste including bitumen residues, contaminated rags, and oily waste must be labeled, stored on impermeable pads for no longer than 90 days, transported only by licensed hazardous waste carriers, and manifested to the EPA within 24 hours of movement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Fire Services Act is mandatory before storage or warehousing operations begin: the premises must pass local Fire Bureau inspection for extinguishers, indoor hydrants, emergency lighting, exit markings, and fire protection equipment. A Public Hazardous Substances and Combustible Materials Permit is required if stored bitumen containers exceed the regulatory quantity threshold. Civil defense and structural load inspection by a certified architect or civil engineer is required for drum racks, container stacking areas, pavement, and warehouse floors. Occupational Safety and Health Administration approval is required for asphalt handling, hot work, confined-space entry, H2S and oxygen gas monitoring, personal protective equipment, and spill response; workers exposed to asphalt fumes must receive health surveillance and periodic safety training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance and its subordinate National Taxation Administration (NTA); regional National Tax Administration offices (Taipei, Northern, Central, Southern, Kaohsiung) administer profit-seeking enterprise tax, business tax, and uniform invoice controls. Online portals: Taiwan Tax Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw) and Electronic Uniform Invoice Integration Service Platform (einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An offshore non-Taiwan corporate entity, including a PRC-incorporated WFOE Limited, must first obtain investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals for non-PRC investors or the cross-strait regulation applicable to mainland-China profit-making enterprises. The entity then registers a branch office or subsidiary under the Taiwan Company Act. Within 15 days after business commencement, the entity must file a profit-seeking enterprise tax registration application with the local National Taxation Administration, attaching the approved investment certificate, company registration certificate, articles of incorporation or charter, proof of the registered place of business, identification of the responsible person and directors, corporate seal records, and Taiwan bank account details. The NTA verifies the application and issues a tax registration certificate containing the eight-digit Unified Business Number (UBI), which is the single taxpayer identification number for income tax, business tax/VAT, customs control, and electronic uniform invoice issuance. A foreign entity with no fixed place of business in Taiwan that supplies only electronic or digital services to Taiwan persons may instead apply online for simplified business tax registration on etax.nat.gov.tw to obtain a UBI and appoint a fiscal representative; however, containerized physical goods such as bitumen imported into Taiwan will be cleared by the Taiwan importer of record, and the offshore seller is not required to hold Taiwan VAT registration solely for the export sale unless it maintains a fixed place of business or a taxable presence in Taiwan.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a Taiwan-registered branch or subsidiary of a foreign WFOE is taxed as a domestic profit-seeking enterprise on Taiwan-source income; a non-resident without a fixed place of business is subject to withholding on Taiwan-source income, and Taiwan does not permit pass-through classification for corporate WFOE structures).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not operate a check-the-box entity classification election or a hybrid mismatch election under the Business Tax Act. The tax classification is determined by the legal form and registration obtained under the Taiwan Company Act; a foreign investor may choose between branch and subsidiary forms, and an entity may voluntarily apply for VAT registration below the statutory threshold, but these are procedural choices, not statutory tax classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act (Taiwan VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For goods, the applicable category for wholesale bitumen, mandatory business tax registration is triggered when average monthly sales exceed NT$80,000; for services, NT$40,000. Foreign e-commerce digital service suppliers are required to register when annual taxable turnover exceeds NT$480,000. General VAT taxpayers with average monthly sales above NT$200,000 must issue uniform invoices and collect VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan does not impose a real-time fiscal approval or anti-fraud digital stamping system. The statutory system is the Electronic Uniform Invoice (EUI) regime. Registered VAT taxpayers issuing electronic uniform invoices must transmit invoice data to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Service Platform or its certified Value-Added Service Centers using the MOF Turnkey integration/API channel. E-invoice data must be transmitted generally within 48 hours after issuance. Anti-fraud controls rely on the mandatory unique uniform invoice number, random check code, carrier registration, and cross-matching of invoice data with customs declarations, bank foreign exchange records, and VAT returns; no separate centralized fiscal stamp is affixed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, exported goods are zero-rated. The registered profit-seeking enterprise must prove that the goods were actually exported from Taiwan customs territory, that the sale was to an overseas buyer, and that the relevant export customs declaration and transport documents support the movement of goods. For containerized bitumen, the cargo must leave Taiwan under a valid customs export declaration and ocean bill of lading or multimodal transport document. Output VAT on a zero-rated export is charged at 0%, and the input VAT attributable to the exported goods is recoverable by credit against other output VAT or by refund under Article 39 of the Business Tax Act, subject to documentary verification by the National Taxation Administration and Customs Administration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs-validated export customs declaration (export entry) issued by Taiwan Customs Administration under the exporter's Unified Business Number
Original or authenticated electronic ocean Bill of Lading, or multimodal transport document, showing the Taiwan port of loading, container number(s), and overseas discharge port
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list describing the bitumen product, HS tariff classification, net and gross weight, and container number(s)
Container freight movement evidence, including container seal numbers and the shipping carrier's container manifest
Bank evidence of export proceeds settlement: inward remittance advice, export foreign exchange settlement certificate, or SWIFT LC/TT payment advice matching the invoice value
Signed sales contract or purchase order evidencing the foreign buyer and the agreed INCOTERM and payment terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan Customs Administration and the National Taxation Administration cross-audit export declarations, bills of lading, container movement records, VAT returns, and bank foreign exchange receipts. If zero-rating is claimed without the complete documented proof, or if export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day statutory period without lawful extension, the zero rate is reversed, VAT at 5% is collected with interest, and any refunded input VAT is clawed back. False or fraudulent export declarations are treated as tax evasion under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, carrying a penalty of five to fifteen times the evaded tax, and may also trigger criminal liability under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act, as well as restriction or suspension of the taxpayer's export declaration and uniform invoice privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a controlled currency regime under PBOC and SAFE. The Renminbi is not freely convertible on the capital account; convertibility is registration-based and transaction-specific. For a Taiwan-invested WFOE, current account trade flows such as import payments and export receivable collections for drummed and containerized bitumen are convertible after the bank completes 'genuineness and consistency' verification against customs declarations and underlying trade documents. Capital account transactions, however, require prior SAFE approval and registration: the initial paid-in capital remitted from Taiwan must be registered as foreign direct investment, credited into a dedicated capital foreign exchange account, and any subsequent conversion from foreign currency to RMB must be supported by a capital payment intention statement and a specific use plan. Profit remittance to Taiwan is permitted only after the statutory annual audit, corporate income tax settlement, and the completion of SAFE profit distribution registration; unresolved inter-company balances or tax liabilities will block the outflow. Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory conversion, but they must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange settlement account and reconciled within the SAFE cross-border receipts and payments monitoring system. The regime therefore reduces liquidity risk when documentary discipline is maintained, but creates material settlement delay when capital registration is incomplete or underlying documents are mismatched.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender ratio applies: 0% of export foreign currency receipts must be converted to RMB. The WFOE must repatriate all export proceeds from containerized bitumen shipments to its domestic foreign exchange settlement account within the standard 90-day export collection period after customs declaration; non-repatriation beyond the 90-day window requires a written extension filed with the designated bank and SAFE before expiry. Foreign currency may remain in the settlement account, and voluntary conversion to RMB is permitted after submission of the sales invoice, customs export declaration, bill of lading, and bank receipt matching.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Foreign Exchange Account (FDI registered) and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Settlement Account and Export Proceeds Collection Account
Import/Export Trade Payment Account and FX Hedging Collateral Account
Secondary Liquidity and Concentration Management Account for China Cash Pooling

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable for the WFOE in Mainland China. Offshore digital EMIs and Taiwan-based non-bank fintech platforms are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE to provide onshore RMB or foreign currency account services, execute SAFE capital account registrations, or settle trade payments against Chinese customs declarations. They cannot serve as the primary clearing entity for this treasury structure. Feasibility rating: Low. They may be used only in ancillary offshore invoicing for non-China legs, and even then transfers to the onshore WFOE must ultimately clear through a licensed Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical branch interview is mandatory. The Mainland WFOE's statutory legal representative or the senior manager appointed as banking mandate holder must appear in person at the selected Tier-1 bank branch for identity verification and corporate purpose confirmation. Taiwan-resident shareholders and directors may appoint a mainland representative through a notarized power of attorney, with the power of attorney authenticated according to cross-strait notarization procedures, but a fully remote consular opening is not permitted. Video-based KYC may be offered by certain banks as a supplementary verification, not as a substitute for the in-branch interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity via multi-tier Taiwanese or Hong Kong holding structure prevents identification of natural persons controlling the WFOE and the source of initial capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association for every entity in the ownership chain; updated Register of Members or UBO registry; Taiwan-notarized shareholder statements; bank reference letters from the Taiwan remitting bank; source of wealth and income documentation covering salaries, dividends, and asset disposals for natural-person ultimate owners; audited financial statements of the Taiwan parent; and a commercial explanation demonstrating why a WFOE is the appropriate vehicle for bitumen and asphalt trading.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flags from drummed bitumen containerization, including over-invoicing or under-invoicing, inconsistent commodity pricing, third-port transshipment, or cash-based settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase and sales contracts with reference to recognized price benchmarks such as Platts or Argus; commercial invoices and packing lists; full-set original bills of lading; Chinese customs export or import declarations; independent pre-shipment inspection certificates issued by CCIC, SGS, or Bureau Veritas; warehouse receipts and terminal storage reports; marine insurance certificates; and bank statements demonstrating direct alignment between payer, beneficiary, and the underlying transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-like substance issues whereby the WFOE has no physical operation, no local employees, or receives funding through circular Taiwan-Hong Kong-Mainland remittance routes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid office or warehouse lease agreement; payroll records and PRC social insurance filings for WFOE employees; corporate bank statements showing ordinary operating expenditures; VAT and corporate income tax filings; board minutes authorizing the bank account opening and trading operations; and ERP or inventory management records evidencing physical handling of asphalt and bitumen products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent capital account usage, including attempted conversion of capital funds into RMB for purposes outside the approved business scope, or commingling of capital funds with trade settlement accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign Direct Investment registration certificate and currency code details; capital account payment intention forms specifying the underlying approved purpose; audited use-of-funds statement; Chinese CPA capital verification report; board resolution approving the cash flow plan; invoices and contracts for each committed capital expenditure; and confirmation that all capital-derived RMB payments are made strictly within the WFOE's approved business scope.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: the Taiwan investor instructs its Taiwan bank to issue an SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's SAFE-registered capital foreign exchange account at a Chinese Tier-1 bank. The beneficiary account must be identified as a capital project account, and the remittance purpose plus SAFE BOP transaction code must read 'foreign direct investment paid-in capital injection', using the code family 601 for direct investment. The Taiwan remitter must be exactly the approved investor in the SAFE FDI registration; funds from unrelated third parties are prohibited. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the transaction in the SAFE digital foreign exchange monitoring database and issues a capital flow record. If RMB is required, the WFOE submits a capital payment intention order, settles the foreign currency into RMB, and disburses funds only against a directors' resolution and underlying transaction documentation. The Chinese CPA must issue a capital verification report for commercial registration and shareholder contribution records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for bitumen and asphalt purchases and sales may use: (1) SWIFT MT103 for low-to-medium-value direct telegraphic transfers supported by commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and customs declarations; (2) irrevocable sight commercial Letters of Credit for high-value containerized cargo, incorporating independent surveyor certificates and quality specifications; and (3) documentary collections under D/P or D/A terms where the buyer-seller relationship has established trade history. Every payment must be classified in the bank's goods trade payment system with the appropriate SAFE current account transaction code, and the bank will match the foreign exchange payment to the relevant customs declaration in the cross-border receipts and payments system before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts, non-speculative, backed by signed import or export contracts and invoices, typically with tenors up to 12 months.
CNY/USD FX swaps for genuine liquidity and cash flow management, requiring two-leg settlement and SAFE documentary support, with no synthetic leveraged positions.
Vanilla CNY/USD call and put options with premium payments, subject to real-demand verification; exotic or barrier structures are not permitted.

Onshore cross-currency interest rate swaps are permissible only when the underlying foreign currency debt is SAFE-registered, and they are limited to hedging the corresponding interest and principal exposure.

Offshore NDFs are not permitted in the onshore WFOE treasury; Mainland China regulated banks do not offer deliverable NDF products to onshore non-financial entities, and any Taiwan-bank NDF arrangement must not be used to settle, convert, or anticipate RMB cash flows without onshore SAFE registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Report (annual report) under the PRC Regulations on Enterprise Information Disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, shared with MOFCOM and SAFE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year from 1 January through 30 June covering the immediately preceding fiscal year ended 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion in the Operating Abnormal List; after three consecutive years of non-filing, placement on the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List with credit blacklisting, procurement, banking, tax refund and cross-border remittance restrictions; in aggravated cessation cases SAMR may revoke the business licence and initiate administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Information Report under the PRC Foreign Investment Law and the Interim Measures on Foreign Investment Information Reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce and municipal commerce authorities through the SAMR-integrated national annual report system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same annual window as the SAMR annual report: 1 January to 30 June for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Order to rectify followed by administrative fine of CNY 100,000 to CNY 500,000 if correction is refused; inclusion in the abnormal operations list; SAFE may suspend foreign exchange settlement, profit remittance and foreign debt/capital account processing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement of Liabilities and annual corporate income tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration and the local competent tax authority of the WFOE registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of each fiscal year, no later than 31 May; quarterly prepayment returns due within 15 days after each quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid or unreported tax; possible immigration exit restriction on the responsible officer; criminal liability for fraudulent annual returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and independent CPA audit report prepared, approved by shareholders and retained for statutory inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained by the company and presented to shareholders; financial data incorporated in the SAMR annual report and MOFCOM foreign investment information report; available to tax authorities on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements prepared within four months after year-end; audit report completed before the 30 June annual report deadline and before the 31 May CIT annual return filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to comply with the PRC Company Law audit obligation exposes the company and responsible officers to fines; the annual report cannot be validly completed without audited financial information; false or omitted disclosure may trigger abnormal listing, tax penalties and disciplinary action against the CPA firm.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic tax and payroll statutory returns covering VAT, individual income tax, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duty, social insurance and housing fund
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration, local social insurance bureaus and housing fund management centres
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT and surcharge returns due by the 15th day of the following month or the 15th day after quarter-end; monthly payroll IIT and social contributions due by the 15th day; annual IIT consolidated settlement for employees due by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CNY 2,000 per return, increased to CNY 2,000 to CNY 10,000 for aggravated cases; late payment interest of 0.05% per day; outstanding income tax withholding and social insurance amounts recoverable with administrative enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign exchange direct investment information confirmation and FDI capital flow validation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the designated receiving bank; data derived from the SAMR annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted through the SAMR annual report window by 30 June; any equity, capital or control change involving foreign exchange must be reported to SAFE through the bank within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Foreign exchange administrative fines up to CNY 300,000 for non-compliant reporting; suspension of foreign exchange settlement, dividend repatriation and subsequent capital contributions; inclusion in SAFE blacklist affecting all cross-border payments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Taiwan investor-side annual declaration of approved mainland China investment operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, for the Taiwanese direct investor holding the China WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration generally due by 30 June covering the prior calendar year; shareholding, capital and operational scope changes must be reported to MOEAIC within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure by the Taiwanese investor may trigger penalties under the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, including fines, revocation of investment approval and mandatory disposal of the mainland China investment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No quantitative balance-sheet, turnover or headcount exemption applies to a PRC WFOE. PRC Company Law makes independent CPA audit mandatory for every registered limited liability company; the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise implementation rules and the Foreign Investment Law reinforce the audit-backed annual information report. Quantitative size metrics such as total assets exceeding CNY 300 million, annual revenue exceeding CNY 300 million or staff exceeding 200 only affect disclosure classification, supervision intensity and parent consolidation requirements; they do not create the audit duty because the duty already exists at zero threshold from incorporation onward.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises, otherwise known as China GAAP or ASBE, substantially converged with IFRS. Small-enterprise accounting standards are generally unavailable or unsuitable for a foreign-invested wholesale trading entity with group reporting requirements; the Taiwan parent consolidation may require IFRS as adopted in Taiwan.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: PRC: no central public UBO register filing is required, but the WFOE must annually confirm and update shareholder, paid-in capital, equity structure and ultimate controller information in the SAMR annual report by 30 June; any shareholding transfer or capital change must be registered with SAMR within 30 days, reported through the foreign investment information system and, if involving cross-border funds, filed through the bank with SAFE within 30 days. Taiwan shareholder side: the Taiwanese investor must maintain current MOEAIC approval and file the annual mainland China investment declaration by 30 June; any equity transfer or structural change in the China WFOE is reportable to MOEAIC within 30 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 for a registered address and corporate secretarial support service in a mainstream PRC commercial centre
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 8,000 for an independent PRC CPA audit of a low-risk wholesale bitumen and asphalt trading WFOE with containerized logistics, depending on transaction volume, intercompany balances and consolidation scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan levies a 20% Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax; the Alternative Minimum Tax is 12% on prescribed basic income; unappropriated earnings retained beyond legal limits incur a 5% retained-earnings surcharge; R&D expenditure may qualify for investment tax credits under the Statute for Industrial Innovation; no zero-tax free-zone or patent-box holiday applies to a wholesale bitumen/asphalt logistics trader, and preferential incentives are generally unavailable to a pure distributor without substantive manufacturing or qualifying strategic-industry activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Taiwan Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form 112) filed electronically through the Ministry of Finance TaxPAY e-filing portal or through an approved tax agent filing system; supplemental withholding statements for payments to non-residents are filed separately through the National Tax Administration withholding system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, with semi-annual provisional tax payments (estimated payments) during the fiscal year; the annual Form 112 reconciliation is filed once per fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar fiscal year ending 31 December, Form 112 must be filed from 1 May through 31 May of the following year; a fiscal-year non-calendar taxpayer must file within five months after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and gross operating revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwanese WFOE is a Taiwan tax resident and must report worldwide revenue; all bitumen/asphalt containerized wholesale revenue, including export sales and local Taiwan sales, must be included; if the WFOE merely issues invoices and all principal trading functions are performed abroad, Taiwan tax authorities may recharacterize the entity as a sham or agency and impose withholding on the true non-resident owner.

Deduct only documented volume rebates, quality claims, and container-return credits; related-party discounts must be supported by written contracts and must satisfy the arm's length standard; any discount granted to an affiliated mainland China buyer without commercial justification will be treated as a constructive dividend or non-deductible transfer pricing adjustment.

This net figure is used in the business-tax reconciliation and in the transfer pricing ratio; net sales must agree with the VAT/issuance register and customs export declarations; if the WFOE reports net sales that are disproportionately low relative to freight, storage, and logistics activity, this triggers a Taiwanese economic-substance audit.

Include actual landing cost of drummed and bagged penetration-grade bitumen: purchase price, ocean freight, marine insurance, Taiwan customs duties, stevedoring, terminal storage, and container transport; related-party purchases from mainland China suppliers must be supported by CUP or TNMM analysis; costs lacking valid invoices, customs entries, or title-transfer evidence are non-deductible and may be reclassified as loans or dividends.

The gross margin must be reconciled to the taxpayer's management accounts and compared to Taiwan wholesale petroleum and asphalt-distribution comparables; an abnormally low gross profit earned by a fully staffed Taiwan logistics entity while the mainland China parent captures most residual profit is a fatal transfer-pricing red flag.

Itemize wages, terminal rentals, insurance, freight forwarding, quality-testing, bank charges, communication, and professional fees; management fees and allocated head-office charges paid or accrued to a non-resident parent are deductible only if the service was actually rendered, the fee is arm's length, Taiwanese withholding tax is paid, and the payer retains contemporaneous evidence; fees with no sustained benefit are treated as hidden profit distributions and are disallowed.

This is the key operative-income line for the Taiwan TNMM examination; the WFOE must show that its operating margin falls within the interquartile range of approved wholesale bitumen comparables; below-range operating profits, especially with continuous losses funded by the foreign shareholder, invite transfer-pricing adjustment and capital-contribution recharacterization.

Include foreign-exchange gains, scrap sales, interest income, indemnities, and disposal gains on logistics assets; foreign-source interest and deemed royalty income must be separately identified for foreign tax credit purposes; a non-resident shareholder with an offshore loan to the WFOE must support interest income by a loan agreement and proof of remittance; unpaid interest is subject to 20% non-resident withholding.

Include bad debts, inventory losses, container demurrage penalties, and asset losses; all losses must be evidenced by official documents, court judgments, collection/closing protocols, or customs destruction certificates; losses from transactions with a non-resident related party are scrutinized as possible transfers of income to overseas related companies.

Total profit must tie directly to the audited or certified financial statements; any increase or decrease required by Taiwanese transfer-pricing adjustments, withholding tax liabilities, or tax-disallowed expenditures must be recorded in the reconciliation schedule; a WFOE sustained solely by foreign parent loans with no independent equity will be viewed as a conduit.

Deduct only assessed and formally accepted prior-year operating losses within the 10-year carryforward window; if the WFOE has not met economic-substance tests and its losses were caused by non-arm's-length purchases from the mainland China parent, the loss deduction will be denied and adjusted profit will be taxed at 20%.

A bitumen wholesaler normally reports no significant tax-exempt income; if tax-exempt amounts are claimed, the taxpayer bears the burden of proof under the Movement of Income Tax Act; illegal treaty-shopping or shell arrangements using an exempt parent entity do not reduce Taiwan taxable income and trigger Article 43-1 anti-avoidance recharacterization.

Compute taxable income after all adjustments; for a WFOE with non-resident owners, ensure no unrecorded deemed dividend or loan-back transaction has been made to the foreign shareholder; taxable income, once assessed, becomes the basis for the 20% corporate income tax and any retained-earnings surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at 20% and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 20% statutory rate and subtract only legal Taiwan tax credits; foreign tax credits for mainland China taxes paid on cross-border bitumen transactions are capped by the excess Taiwan tax attributable to that foreign-source income; overclaiming foreign tax credits for non-Taiwan-source transactions is a common audit trigger for a cross-strait WFOE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 112 triggers a surcharge of 3% of the unpaid tax for every two-month delay, capped at 10%, plus daily interest on overdue tax arrears under the Tax Collection Act; late payment without filing accrues monthly interest and delinquency penalties; false or fraudulent under-declaration is penalized under Income Tax Act Article 110 with an administrative shortfall penalty of up to two to three times the underpaid tax; willful evasion with fraudulent documents constitutes a criminal offense under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act punishable by imprisonment for up to five years and monetary fines; directors who sign false returns are exposed to joint civil liability and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties paid to a foreign corporate shareholder, the Taiwanese WFOE must, before remittance, submit to the District National Tax Administration: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home jurisdiction tax authority for the relevant taxable year; (2) a beneficial-ownership declaration and supporting substance documentation proving the shareholder is not a conduit, agent, or nominee; (3) the original financing, license, sales, or shareholding agreement; (4) the withholding-tax remittance form and a formal written application for reduced withholding or exemption; (5) a power of attorney for any local tax representative. Where the shareholder is resident in Mainland China, relief is governed by the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement where effective; the same TRC and beneficial-ownership protocol applies, and the mainland shareholder must obtain an authentic mainland tax resident certificate and pass the economic-substance / Core Income-Generating Activity test before the 21% dividend withholding can be reduced.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Taiwan withholding tax on non-resident payees is 21% for dividends, 20% for interest, and 20% for royalties; treaty-covered interest and royalties are frequently reduced to 10% under Taiwan's bilateral conventions, and licensing payments that are not true royalties may be recast as service fees or dividends; a WFOE paying interest to a parent must prove the loan exists, the funds were actually remitted, the rate is arm's length, and the Taiwan interest is subject to the full 20% mechanism if no treaty relief applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Taiwanese WFOE is required to prepare a Local File transfer-pricing report when its annual controlled related-party transactions exceed NT$300 million, and a Master File when the group-wide related-party transaction or consolidated-turnover criteria prescribed by the Ministry of Finance are met; Country-by-Country reporting is separately required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above the NT$27 billion statutory threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not apply a Gulf-state-style Economic Substance Regulation, but the tax administration applies OECD-aligned substance, beneficial-ownership, and Core Income-Generating Activity (CIGA) tests; for a WFOE trading bitumen on a containerized wholesale basis, economic substance in Taiwan requires a physical place of management, local operational staff performing procurement, logistics control, risk assumption, sales negotiation, invoicing, storage decisions, and independent corporate governance; if those functions are performed by the mainland China parent and the Taiwan entity is merely a pass-through invoice, remittance, or bank-account shell, Taiwan will disregard the corporate form, deny treaty benefits, reattribute taxable profit, impose a 21% constructive-dividend withholding tax, and apply tax evasion penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting bitumen/containerized asphalt sales, creating fictitious related-party invoices above the actual purchase price, concealing offshore bank accounts, or filing Form 112 with false inventory, customs, and shipping records to erase or reduce Taiwan taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 110 authorizes penalty of up to two to three times the understated tax; Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act criminalizes willful tax evasion with fraudulent means, carrying imprisonment for up to five years and fine; the tax authority also charges overdue-interest penalties and may blacklist the entity for non-payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign a false return or order the creation of fake logistics documents may have the corporate veil pierced; they are personally and jointly liable for civil restitution of the underpaid tax, assets in their names can be frozen, bank accounts and overseas travel are blocked by the National Tax Administration blacklisting, and they face criminal imprisonment with possible disqualification from holding office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Taiwanese WFOE with no real office, officers or employees in Taiwan, with board meetings held abroad, bitumen title never passing through Taiwan, contracts negotiated entirely by the mainland China parent, and the Taiwan entity existing solely to receive payments and route profits to the foreign shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will disregard the Taiwan entity under Income Tax Act Article 43-1 and anti-abuse case law, deny intercompany deductions, reclassify remittances as taxable Taiwan-source income, apply a 21% deemed-dividend withholding, impose understatement penalties up to three times the tax, and report the shell structure to the competent customs and company registries for compulsory deregistration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors are treated as de facto owners of the sham; they are strictly liable for the unpaid withholding and corporate income tax, lose limited liability where corporate formalities are ignored, face civil seizure of personal assets, travel bans preventing departure from Taiwan, and criminal liability for fraudulent incorporation if they signed false declarations of substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Evasion / Money-Laundering-Style Cross-Border Payment Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in massive intercompany sales of bitumen asphalt to a mainland China parent or offshore affiliate at deliberately below-viable prices, paying grossly inflated management or royalty charges, and receiving SWIFT LC/TT wire proceeds without real trade documentation, customs entries, bill-of-lading matches, or independent economic purpose; the pattern is reported as AML red-flag activity and enables base-erosion profit stripping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taiwan's Transfer Pricing Regulations permit full recharacterization and repricing to the arm's length margin; the adjustment is subject to Income Tax Act Article 110 penalty of two to three times the resulting tax shortfall, plus a 21% withholding on deemed dividends; Money Laundering Control Act penalties attach to fraudulent trade-payment schemes with imprisonment and substantial fines; false trade documents also expose the WFOE to customs and banking-law sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or benefit from the transfer-pricing strip are jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax, penalties, and withholding; personal assets derived from the scheme are subject to confiscation; civil restitution to the Ministry of Finance is ordered; the directors may be placed on an immigration blacklist and detained at the border; and criminal sentences under the Tax Collection Act and Money Laundering Control Act can result in imprisonment for five years or more where the scheme is organized.
